facts.label: Bottom line
facts.text: Ziff Davis held more cash than debt at the end of the third quarter of 2026 after selling Connectivity, which cushions creditors near term, but earnings-based leverage on the continuing business cannot be calculated from the filings. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against comfort is on earnings, not on the balance sheet: the continuing business reported an operating loss of USD 75.4 million for nine months 2026, net advertising revenue retention fell in all three advertising segments between the third quarters of 2025 and 2026, and subscription customer counts fell in all three subscription segments. The net cash position is a one-time result of the sale, so a durable view needs last-twelve-months EBITDA on the continuing basis, which no filing prints yet. The view would improve if recast full-year 2025 figures show EBITDA that comfortably covers the remaining notes and interest, and would weaken if buybacks, acquisitions or the tax payment on the sale gain used up the cash balance, which stood at USD 1,407.7 million at quarter-end before the 1.75% repayment. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 54–55; calculation C79; calculation C60

Basis: 10-Q_2026-03-31_zd-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-06-30_zd-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22 - The issuer states no EBITDA or adjusted EBITDA in any period, so EBITDA (Reported) is derived as operating income plus depreciation and amortization, includes goodwill impairments and has no adjusted twin; the EBITDA bridge is therefore not stated (Medium). A company reconciliation or the covenant definition would close it. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_zd-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 128–129; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29 - The covenant levels of the Credit Agreement are printed but the reported leverage and coverage ratios and the EBITDA definitions behind them are not, so covenant headroom is not calculable (High for covenant work). The executed credit agreement and a compliance certificate would close it. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 33–34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 28–29 - The 1.75% convertible notes were repaid after September 30, 2026, but the filing gives no repayment date, no interest paid and no pro forma balances, so every figure of the post-balance-sheet table is not supplied (Medium). A current report or the next quarterly report would close it. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 73 - The revolver matures on the earlier of June 18, 2027 or an earlier date under limited circumstances that did not occur, seven months after the as-of date, and no extension is disclosed; availability of USD 348.9 million is net of letters of credit whose amount is not printed separately (Medium). A later filing stating an extension or replacement and the letters-of-credit amount would close it. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 33–34; calculation C85 - Income taxes payable of USD 130.8 million at quarter-end, up because of the tax on the sale gain, have no printed payment date, so their effect on cash after the balance-sheet date is not established (Medium). The next quarterly report would close it. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 72; calculation C68 - Cash of USD 158.6 million is held in foreign jurisdictions; the 2025 annual report says foreign earnings are treated as permanently reinvested or remittable substantially free of additional taxes and that the tax cost of repatriating them is not practicable to determine, so the access cost of this cash is not established (Low). The liquidity analysis should treat it as cash with an unstated access cost. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 73; 10-K_2025-12-31_zd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 181; calculation C83 - The balance sheet at September 30, 2025 is not in the sources, so the nine-month 2025 columns have no balance-sheet pair and net debt for that date is not supplied (Low). The September 2025 quarterly report would close it. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3 - The notes are described as guaranteed on an unsecured basis by certain domestic wholly-owned subsidiaries and the revolver as secured by the guarantors' assets, but no guarantor is named and the two convertible issues state no subsidiary guarantee, so the debt stack states obligors only as printed (Medium for structural analysis). The executed documents and the list of subsidiaries would close it. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33 - Statement lines the issuer prints only in some periods are written as not supplied in the other columns: the loss on sale of businesses, gains and credit-loss provisions on investments and the net income split on the income statement, the held-for-sale balance-sheet lines, and the debt payment line of the cash flow statement; a printed dash is also written as not supplied and never as zero (Low). No action is needed beyond reading the filing's own presentation. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_zd-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 128–129; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–4 - The cash flow table reproduces the totals and the lines that matter for credit, being net income, depreciation, share-based compensation, impairment, the gain or loss on sale, deferred tax, capital expenditure, acquisitions, disposals, debt payment and repurchases; the remaining non-cash adjustments and working-capital lines are in the filings and are summed as a calculated working-capital change instead of being reproduced one by one (Low). The filings themselves hold the lines. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_zd-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 129–130; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4 - The revolver's drawn spread and any floor are not stated because nothing is drawn, only the margin ranges are printed, and the revolver's scheduled amortisation is not stated (Low). The executed credit agreement would close it. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33 - Claims outside the debt figure are not in Total Debt and are not netted in net debt: future minimum operating lease payments of USD 31.0 million at quarter-end, indirect tax reserves of USD 17.3 million, a liability for uncertain tax positions of USD 19.1 million, settlement payables, revenue-sharing minimum guarantees and cloud and similar commitments whose amounts are not printed, and litigation for which no material loss is accrued; the filings disclose no finance leases, factoring, supplier finance, securitization, defined benefit pension or retiree medical obligations, and the only retirement plan described is a defined contribution 401(k) plan (Low). The amounts that are not printed would close the gap. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 35–37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 73; 10-K_2025-12-31_zd-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 173–175; 10-K_2025-12-31_zd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 191

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against caution is the balance sheet and the absence of an owner with an extraction incentive. Cash exceeded debt principal by USD 535.39 million, the USD 350.0 million revolving facility was undrawn with USD 348.9 million available, no dividend was paid in 2023, 2024 or 2025, free cash flow was USD 287.87 million in FY2025 with Connectivity included, controls over financial reporting were effective with an unqualified audit opinion, and the related-party note discloses one fund investment that needs no further capital. The view would improve if management committed the sale proceeds to debt reduction or a stated minimum cash balance, or if recast continuing results showed stable advertising revenue and positive free cash flow. It would weaken if repurchases continue at the nine-month pace, because finishing the remaining authorization at September's average price would use USD 327.84 million, 61.23% of the cash above debt principal, while taxes of USD 130.8 million are payable and the revolving facility matures on 2027-06-18, or if acquisitions return to the 2024 scale funded from sale cash. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: - Refinancing risk is manageable but concentrated in 2027 and 2028, and the market prices the 2030 senior notes below par. The USD 350.0 million secured revolving facility is undrawn, has USD 348.9 million available, which implies USD 1.1 million of letters of credit, and expires seven months after the as-of date with no extension disclosed. The 2028 convertible notes of USD 263.1 million convert at USD 100 a share against a September average repurchase price of USD 54.93, so repayment in cash at maturity is the likely path. The disclosed fair value of the 2030 senior notes was 91.25% of principal at September 30, 2026 against 94.50% at the 2025 year end, despite the cash build, while the 2028 convertible notes stood at 101.82%; these are fair values disclosed at the period ends from quoted prices or dealer quotes, not current quotations. Noteholders are unsecured and rank behind the secured revolver, which is undrawn; the 2028 convertible notes are also structurally junior to all subsidiary liabilities, while the 2030 senior notes carry guarantees from certain domestic subsidiaries. Generative AI may reduce referral traffic, and the law on its use of copyrighted material is unsettled, which could cut revenue or, if the company's lawsuits succeed, add recoveries that the filings do not size. Privacy class actions against Mashable and IGN under California and federal privacy statutes carry no estimable loss and none is accrued, so an adverse ruling would be an unreserved call on cash. Advertising budgets are cyclical and discretionary, and the company notes that trade and tariff policy can cause cancellations. Interest rates are higher than when the notes were issued, and the company says it may not be able to refinance fixed-rate debt at similar rates. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The downside begins with a further loss of search and AI referral traffic, the risk the company names for its audience and the pressure it cites for the Technology & Shopping decline, together with advertiser budget cuts that the one-year, cancellable agreements allow. The first operating break is in Technology & Shopping and Health & Wellness, where the reporting units with no excess fair value sit: advertising revenue falls faster than the 6.30% of nine months while the cost base, which rose 4.39%, stays near current levels, so EBITDA before goodwill impairment falls below the USD 41.6 million of the third quarter. The financial transmission is further non-cash impairments from the USD 872.8 million of goodwill with little or no headroom, lower covenant earnings if impairments are not added back, and free cash flow that stays negative as in the third quarter, when the combined outflow after capital expenditure was USD 100.07 million. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The liquidity consequence arrives through cash: at the third-quarter rate of fall of USD 198.4 million cash would last 7.09 quarters before the USD 279.95 million of near claims, so continued repurchases with a negative operating cash flow would leave the 2028 convertible notes of USD 263.1 million to be met from a much smaller cash balance, an illustration and not a forecast. The leverage and refinancing consequence is that the revolver would need to be extended in mid-2027 on a covenant package tested against lower earnings, and debt principal is already at least 3.64x the only earnings bound available. Management has several levers: it can stop repurchases, which were USD 92.0 million in the third quarter, cut sales and marketing of USD 363.6 million, defer capital expenditure, repay or repurchase notes below par, or sell further businesses. Resilience is sufficient to avoid liquidity distress within 24 months because those levers are within management's control and cash is large; it is not sufficient if repurchases and acquisitions continue while earnings fall. Observable triggers are advertising retention below 85%, quarterly EBITDA before goodwill impairment below USD 41.6 million, cash below USD 1,000 million, no revolver extension by March 2027, and repurchases above USD 92.0 million in a quarter. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Ziff Davis presents an adequate business profile supported by cash of USD 535.4 million above debt principal, with pro forma cash after the 1.75% repayment not established, an undrawn revolver, fixed-rate unsecured debt with no drawn maturity before March 2028 after that repayment, and no sponsor or dividend, but credit quality is constrained by shrinking, cancellable advertising revenue, a margin that fell to 17.35% from 23.59% before goodwill impairment, USD 872.8 million of goodwill with little or no headroom and a policy of returning cash to shareholders. Cash-flow durability appears weak because free cash flow was an outflow of USD 49.3 million for nine months on the combined basis and 69.91% of EBITDA converted to free cash flow only in FY2025 with Connectivity included. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on extending the revolver before its June 2027 expiry, on earnings recovering in the fourth quarter, and on how much of the sale cash remains by March 2028. The primary downside path is traffic and advertiser losses that lower earnings while cash is spent. A comparison with typical leveraged-credit issuers in the sector is not established because no peer set is supplied. Further analysis would require recast continuing-basis annual results, the executed credit agreement and covenant definitions, the date and effect of the 1.75% repayment and tax payment, and management guidance. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: shareholder returns and falling advertising earnings eroding the sale cash before the 2028 convertible notes and the revolver renewal. ## Request

This source-readiness review covers Ziff Davis, Inc. (issuer zd-1084048), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is five periodic SEC filings, two annual reports and three 2026 quarterly reports, assessed for Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit work. It draws no credit conclusion.

## Findings
### Bottom line

The five supplied filings give creditors a primary-source base for financial, business and fundamental credit work on Ziff Davis, Inc., but they cannot test covenant headroom, ratings or legal priority, so those questions stay open until further documents arrive. Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit can proceed on these filings alone, each with the limitations below.

The main limit is a break in perimeter. The Connectivity business was sold on June 17, 2026; the three 2026 quarterly reports present its results as discontinued and restate the December 31, 2025 balance sheet, while the 2025 annual report still includes it and the 2026 cash flow statements mix continuing and discontinued operations. Full-year 2025 figures on the continuing basis are therefore not printed. No executed indenture or credit agreement, credit rating or company-defined adjusted earnings measure is supplied, board and ownership detail sits in a proxy statement that is not supplied, and the 1.75% convertible notes were repaid after September 30, 2026 on a date the filing does not state.

spans.text: # Financial foundation: Ziff Davis, Inc.
## Request

Financial foundation for Ziff Davis, Inc. (issuer zd-1084048), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is five periodic SEC filings covering FY2024, FY2025 and the first three quarters of 2026, from which it builds statement tables, debt, liquidity and ratio figures with their limits. It makes no credit recommendation.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2024-12-31_zd-20241231.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024 | 2025-02-25 | 34cc74388538f2f4a77d3b02cf577fcd1726892be88241baa84e31353599221c | FY2024 statements and notes, corroborating the 2024 comparatives of the later annual report; segment note and debt note at 2024-12-31; supplemental interest paid for 2024. |

| 10-K_2025-12-31_zd-20251231.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025 | 2026-02-24 | d82766f93eadef9bafeb5a91423f8942ba02db7850899205e700ef59d2e7e2bb | FY2025 and FY2024 statements, debt note and maturity table, credit agreement summary, lease note, segment note, supplemental cash flow data, risk wording on ratings. |

| 10-Q_2026-03-31_zd-20260331.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2026 | 2026-05-08 | b4383d6b9598b810b9fb3f348d468595542218f10a6d14be016ba11e0ba584b2 | First-quarter 2026 and 2025 statements on the recast basis, first-quarter debt note, supplemental interest paid. |

| Supplied analysis | Module | Exact sha256 | Use |

| Source readiness | CP-0 | 3ecaca04a891dd168fe58b08b6d62a507fe4e2152b59da9b1576a6e624d7f1ed | Identity, period and perimeter map, the effective-source set and the limitations on legal documents, ratings, covenant definitions and the Connectivity perimeter break. |
## Findings
### Bottom line

Ziff Davis held more cash than debt at the end of the third quarter of 2026 after selling Connectivity, which cushions creditors near term, but earnings-based leverage on the continuing business cannot be calculated from the filings. Cash was USD 1,407.7 million against carrying-value debt of USD 868.2 million, a net cash position of USD 539.5 million, and the revolving credit facility was undrawn with USD 348.9 million available. At the 2025 year end, before the sale, net debt was USD 259.5 million, or 0.63x EBITDA of USD 411.8 million, derived from operating income and depreciation and including Connectivity.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-K_2025-12-31_zd-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 128–129; calculation C60; calculation C61; calculation C62; calculation C63; calculation C64

The cushion is not recurring cash generation: free cash flow for nine months 2026 was an outflow of USD 49.3 million on a combined basis, and income taxes payable of USD 130.8 million were owed at quarter-end. The 1.75% convertible notes of USD 149.1 million were repaid after quarter-end, leaving notes of USD 723.2 million due in 2028 and 2030.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 48; calculation C70; calculation C68; calculation C65; calculation C87
### Key findings

- The sale of Connectivity turned net debt into net cash but cut reported earnings: EBITDA on the continuing basis was USD 62.0 million for nine months 2026 against USD 188.6 million a year earlier, after goodwill impairments of USD 84.4 million and USD 17.6 million that are not added back, on revenue of USD 843.7 million against USD 874.2 million. Proceeds net of cash divested were USD 1,134.1 million.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C73; calculation C74; calculation C75; calculation C76; calculation C77; calculation C78; calculation C69

- Liquidity is strong at the balance sheet date but rests on the sale: over the same nine months the company repurchased shares for USD 265.0 million and bought property and equipment for USD 91.1 million, and combined operating cash flow in the third quarter was an outflow of USD 77.1 million.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_zd-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C72; calculation C84; calculation C71

- Debt is simple: after the repayment of the 1.75% notes the remaining principal is the 2028 convertible notes of USD 263.1 million and the 2030 senior notes of USD 460.0 million, all fixed rate and unsecured; cash at quarter-end, before the repayment of the 1.75% notes and before taxes payable, exceeded that principal by USD 684.5 million. The revolver commitment of USD 350.0 million is secured, undrawn and matures seven months after the as-of date with no extension disclosed.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 28–33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 77; calculation C66; calculation C67; calculation C86; calculation C85

- A non-debt float is part of the cash story: settlement payables to gift-card customers sit inside accounts payable, not debt, and fell from USD 469.1 million at the 2025 year end to USD 199.6 million at quarter-end, a fall of USD 269.5 million; the filing does not say how much cash is held against them.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; calculation C81; calculation C80; calculation C82

- Leverage and cover can be stated only for the two year ends on the pre-sale perimeter: total debt over EBITDA was 2.65x at the 2024 year end and 2.10x at the 2025 year end, and EBITDA over cash interest was 11.28x and 11.89x; neither is stated for 2026 because no filing prints continuing full-year figures.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_zd-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 128–129; 10-K_2025-12-31_zd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 196; calculation C48; calculation C51
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against comfort is on earnings, not on the balance sheet: the continuing business reported an operating loss of USD 75.4 million for nine months 2026, net advertising revenue retention fell in all three advertising segments between the third quarters of 2025 and 2026, and subscription customer counts fell in all three subscription segments. The net cash position is a one-time result of the sale, so a durable view needs last-twelve-months EBITDA on the continuing basis, which no filing prints yet. The view would improve if recast full-year 2025 figures show EBITDA that comfortably covers the remaining notes and interest, and would weaken if buybacks, acquisitions or the tax payment on the sale gain used up the cash balance, which stood at USD 1,407.7 million at quarter-end before the 1.75% repayment.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 54–55; calculation C79; calculation C60

## Gaps

- Full-year 2025 and last-twelve-months figures on the continuing basis are not printed, so Total debt / EBITDA, Net debt / EBITDA and EBITDA / cash interest at September 30, 2026 are not calculable, and the fourth quarter of 2025 on the continuing basis is not stated in the revenue and EBITDA chart. The 2025 annual report includes Connectivity while the 2026 reports exclude it, so the last-twelve-months construction is not comparable (High). Closing it needs recast full-year 2025 continuing results from a later filing or a lender presentation.

- The 2026 cash flow statements combine continuing and discontinued operations and do not print the operating cash flow of Connectivity, so continuing operating cash flow and free cash flow for nine months 2026 are not directly sourced and are shown on the combined basis (High). The operating cash flow of the discontinued business from a later filing would close it.

- The issuer states no EBITDA or adjusted EBITDA in any period, so EBITDA (Reported) is derived as operating income plus depreciation and amortization, includes goodwill impairments and has no adjusted twin; the EBITDA bridge is therefore not stated (Medium). A company reconciliation or the covenant definition would close it.

- The covenant levels of the Credit Agreement are printed but the reported leverage and coverage ratios and the EBITDA definitions behind them are not, so covenant headroom is not calculable (High for covenant work). The executed credit agreement and a compliance certificate would close it.

- The 1.75% convertible notes were repaid after September 30, 2026, but the filing gives no repayment date, no interest paid and no pro forma balances, so every figure of the post-balance-sheet table is not supplied (Medium). A current report or the next quarterly report would close it.

- The revolver matures on the earlier of June 18, 2027 or an earlier date under limited circumstances that did not occur, seven months after the as-of date, and no extension is disclosed; availability of USD 348.9 million is net of letters of credit whose amount is not printed separately (Medium). A later filing stating an extension or replacement and the letters-of-credit amount would close it.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 33–34; calculation C85

- Income taxes payable of USD 130.8 million at quarter-end, up because of the tax on the sale gain, have no printed payment date, so their effect on cash after the balance-sheet date is not established (Medium). The next quarterly report would close it.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 72; calculation C68

- Cash of USD 158.6 million is held in foreign jurisdictions; the 2025 annual report says foreign earnings are treated as permanently reinvested or remittable substantially free of additional taxes and that the tax cost of repatriating them is not practicable to determine, so the access cost of this cash is not established (Low). The liquidity analysis should treat it as cash with an unstated access cost.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 73; 10-K_2025-12-31_zd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 181; calculation C83

- The balance sheet at September 30, 2025 is not in the sources, so the nine-month 2025 columns have no balance-sheet pair and net debt for that date is not supplied (Low). The September 2025 quarterly report would close it.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3

- The notes are described as guaranteed on an unsecured basis by certain domestic wholly-owned subsidiaries and the revolver as secured by the guarantors' assets, but no guarantor is named and the two convertible issues state no subsidiary guarantee, so the debt stack states obligors only as printed (Medium for structural analysis). The executed documents and the list of subsidiaries would close it.

- Statement lines the issuer prints only in some periods are written as not supplied in the other columns: the loss on sale of businesses, gains and credit-loss provisions on investments and the net income split on the income statement, the held-for-sale balance-sheet lines, and the debt payment line of the cash flow statement; a printed dash is also written as not supplied and never as zero (Low). No action is needed beyond reading the filing's own presentation.

- The cash flow table reproduces the totals and the lines that matter for credit, being net income, depreciation, share-based compensation, impairment, the gain or loss on sale, deferred tax, capital expenditure, acquisitions, disposals, debt payment and repurchases; the remaining non-cash adjustments and working-capital lines are in the filings and are summed as a calculated working-capital change instead of being reproduced one by one (Low). The filings themselves hold the lines.

- The revolver's drawn spread and any floor are not stated because nothing is drawn, only the margin ranges are printed, and the revolver's scheduled amortisation is not stated (Low). The executed credit agreement would close it.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33

- Claims outside the debt figure are not in Total Debt and are not netted in net debt: future minimum operating lease payments of USD 31.0 million at quarter-end, indirect tax reserves of USD 17.3 million, a liability for uncertain tax positions of USD 19.1 million, settlement payables, revenue-sharing minimum guarantees and cloud and similar commitments whose amounts are not printed, and litigation for which no material loss is accrued; the filings disclose no finance leases, factoring, supplier finance, securitization, defined benefit pension or retiree medical obligations, and the only retirement plan described is a defined contribution 401(k) plan (Low). The amounts that are not printed would close the gap.

spans.text: # Business & governance: Ziff Davis, Inc.
## Request

Business and governance fact pack for Ziff Davis, Inc. (issuer zd-1084048), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the five supplied periodic filings covering FY2024, FY2025 and the first three quarters of 2026, used for the business, the Connectivity sale, ownership and control, governance, capital allocation and disclosure. It makes no credit recommendation.
## Sources

| Supplied analysis | Module | Exact sha256 | Use |

| Source readiness | CP-0 | 3ecaca04a891dd168fe58b08b6d62a507fe4e2152b59da9b1576a6e624d7f1ed | Identity, the perimeter break at the Connectivity sale, the effective-source set and the limitations on legal documents, ratings, the proxy statement and guidance. |
## Findings
### Bottom line

Ziff Davis is a publicly listed, advertising-led media company with no controlling shareholder or sponsor stated, so creditors rely on its own cash and earnings rather than owner support, and governance risk rests on how freely it returns cash to shareholders. At September 30, 2026 cash of USD 1,407.7 million exceeded debt principal of USD 872.3 million after the sale of Connectivity for USD 1,200 million, but continuing operations lost USD 75.4 million at the operating line over nine months and USD 265.0 million of cash went to share repurchases.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 73; calculation C67; calculation C68; calculation C69; calculation C70; calculation C45

The remaining business is more exposed to advertising, which was 63.09% of nine-month revenue on contracts that in most cases are short and cancellable, while the Connectivity segment that was sold had supplied 29.68% of FY2025 segment operating income from 15.90% of revenue. The 1.75% convertible notes of USD 149.1 million were repaid after quarter-end on a date the filing does not state; pro forma cash after that repayment is not established.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 53; 10-K_2025-12-31_zd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-K_2025-12-31_zd-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 193–194; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 48; calculation C71; calculation C7; calculation C32; calculation C31
### Key findings

- The remaining business is advertising-led, shrinking and weakening at the profit line. Advertising and performance marketing revenue was USD 532.3 million for nine months 2026, 63.09% of revenue and down 6.30% on the prior year, on advertiser agreements that in most cases run one year or less and can be ended without penalty. The company attributes the Technology & Shopping decline to traffic pressure on affiliate commerce and display advertising, and net advertising retention fell in all three advertising segments between the third quarters of 2025 and 2026. Revenue excluding acquired businesses fell 6.05%, against a reported fall of 3.48%.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 53; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 54–55; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 69; 10-K_2025-12-31_zd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-K_2025-12-31_zd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 49; calculation C72; calculation C7; calculation C12; calculation C19; calculation C13

- Earnings quality has deteriorated, and the impairments show that management lowered its own forecasts for several units. Operating results swung from income of USD 39.7 million to a loss of USD 75.4 million, including goodwill impairments of USD 84.4 million that followed reductions in forecast revenue and earnings in the Health & Wellness and Technology & Shopping units. Excluding goodwill impairment, operating income was USD 8.99 million against USD 57.23 million. Goodwill of USD 872.8 million, 69.21% of the balance, sits in units with no or thin valuation headroom, so further non-cash charges would follow if forecasts slip again. Technology & Shopping and Health & Wellness lost money at segment level for nine months while Cybersecurity & Martech improved.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 56–57; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 70–72; calculation C73; calculation C74; calculation C75; calculation C76; calculation C77; calculation C27

- The sale turned a subscription business with stable margins into cash, and the cash is now open to use by management. The USD 1,200 million price was 15.77x FY2025 segment operating income of USD 76.1 million and 11.41x that figure plus depreciation and amortization, and total proceeds were USD 1,216.1 million including USD 37.0 million held in escrow. Income taxes payable rose by USD 123.5 million to USD 130.8 million, tied by the company to the gain on the sale, with no payment date stated. The business that remains leans more on advertising: advertising was 56.75% of FY2025 revenue with Connectivity and 63.09% for nine months 2026 without it.

### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against caution is the balance sheet and the absence of an owner with an extraction incentive. Cash exceeded debt principal by USD 535.39 million, the USD 350.0 million revolving facility was undrawn with USD 348.9 million available, no dividend was paid in 2023, 2024 or 2025, free cash flow was USD 287.87 million in FY2025 with Connectivity included, controls over financial reporting were effective with an unqualified audit opinion, and the related-party note discloses one fund investment that needs no further capital. The view would improve if management committed the sale proceeds to debt reduction or a stated minimum cash balance, or if recast continuing results showed stable advertising revenue and positive free cash flow. It would weaken if repurchases continue at the nine-month pace, because finishing the remaining authorization at September's average price would use USD 327.84 million, 61.23% of the cash above debt principal, while taxes of USD 130.8 million are payable and the revolving facility matures on 2027-06-18, or if acquisitions return to the 2024 scale funded from sale cash.
### Limitations

- The proxy statement is not supplied, so the conclusion that no controlling shareholder or sponsor is stated cannot be confirmed; a holder above the stated thresholds, a nomination agreement or an activist position would change the reading of capital-return and sale decisions.

- The executed indentures and credit agreement are not supplied, so the finding on room for shareholder returns rests on the debt note summaries; basket sizes, the covenant earnings definition and the guarantor list could change how much cash may legally be distributed.

- FY2025 revenue and segment profit include Connectivity and no full-year continuing figures are printed, so the finding on the shift toward advertising rests on nine-month comparisons; the seasonally stronger fourth quarter could change the advertising share.

- No management presentation, earnings release or guidance figure is supplied, so the finding that forecasts were lowered rests on impairment disclosures alone; management's own outlook could soften or sharpen it.

- The latest document is dated 2026-11-06, so the date and interest of the 1.75% notes repayment and the settlement of the USD 12.0 million working-capital escrow are not established; either could change the size of the cash cushion over debt.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

On 2026-03-02 Ziff Davis agreed to sell its Connectivity business, the Ookla group of broadband testing and insight brands, to Accenture Inc. for an aggregate cash price of USD 1,200 million, subject to customary adjustments, and completed the sale on 2026-06-17. Total proceeds were USD 1,216.1 million, being USD 1,179.1 million at closing plus USD 37.0 million in escrow, and cash received at closing net of USD 45.0 million of cash divested was USD 1,134.1 million. The escrow holds USD 12.0 million for working-capital adjustments, to be settled within 120 days of closing and still a receivable at September 30, 2026, and USD 25.0 million for indemnifications, payable on the earlier of settlement of indemnification matters or three years after closing.

Ziff Davis recorded a pre-tax gain on sale of USD 860.6 million within discontinued operations and elected not to allocate interest expense to the discontinued business. It plans to use the proceeds for general corporate purposes and capital allocation activities, subject to the conditions of its outstanding debt securities, and has not itemized any use beyond share repurchases and the tax on the gain. A transition services agreement has Ziff Davis provide accounting, tax, treasury, technology and human resource services to Accenture for up to twelve months from closing, extendable by two three-month periods, at Connectivity's expense; USD 4.8 million was due from Accenture at quarter-end, and Ziff Davis states it has no other significant involvement with Connectivity.

No new debt was issued in nine months 2026: the cash flow statement shows no borrowing or debt payment, no 4.625% senior notes were repurchased in the period and the revolving credit facility had no balance. The debt stack comes from earlier steps: USD 550.0 million of 1.75% convertible notes issued on 2019-11-15; USD 750.0 million of 4.625% senior notes due 2030 issued on 2020-10-07, of which about USD 289.96 million has since been repurchased, leaving USD 460.04 million; a revolving credit agreement signed on 2021-04-07 and raised to USD 350.0 million on 2024-06-18, with maturity moved to 2027-06-18; and the exchange of 2024-07-16, in which USD 400.9 million of the 1.75% notes was swapped, with certain holders, for USD 263.1 million of 3.625% convertible notes due 2028 plus USD 135.0 million in cash. The remaining USD 149.1 million of 1.75% notes was repaid in cash after September 30, 2026, leaving principal of USD 723.2 million in the 2028 and 2030 notes.

spans.text: # Fundamental credit: Ziff Davis, Inc.
## Request

This synthesis covers Ziff Davis, Inc. (issuer zd-1084048), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the fundamental credit profile of the business after the sale of Connectivity, built from five periodic SEC filings and the supplied source readiness, financial foundation and business and governance analyses. It assigns no rating and makes no security recommendation.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Ziff Davis can meet its debt service from cash for the next 12 months to 24 months, but the cash came from selling Connectivity rather than from earnings, so noteholders depend on management not spending it. Cash was USD 1,407.7 million against debt principal of USD 872.3 million at September 30, 2026, and pro forma cash after the 1.75% convertible notes were repaid after that date is not established.

Earnings fell sharply: nine-month EBITDA was USD 62.0 million against USD 188.6 million a year earlier, and USD 146.4 million against USD 206.2 million before goodwill impairment, while combined free cash flow was an outflow of USD 49.3 million and USD 265.0 million went to share repurchases. The view weakens if repurchases continue at the third-quarter pace.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_zd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-24; calculation CALC-25; calculation CALC-26; calculation CALC-27; calculation CALC-19
### Key findings

- Debt service is covered by cash for the next 12 months to 24 months, and after the 1.75% repayment no drawn debt matures before March 2028. ### Business and ownership read-through

Ziff Davis, Inc. is a Delaware company listed on Nasdaq and run from New York. Since it sold Connectivity on June 17, 2026 it reports four segments, Technology & Shopping, Gaming & Entertainment, Health & Wellness and Cybersecurity & Martech, with nine-month revenue of USD 843.7 million that was 63.09% advertising and performance marketing, 34.97% subscription and licensing and 1.94% other. The credit link is that cash flow visibility is low for the advertising majority, which sits on short, cancellable agreements and on search and social traffic, and moderate for the subscription third, which supports debt service but is not growing: subscription revenue fell 0.38% in nine months while customer counts fell in all three segments that report them. The sale removed the segment that earned 29.68% of FY2025 segment operating income from 15.90% of revenue, so the remaining group is more exposed to advertising than the group that issued the notes.

### Revenue drivers and pricing power

The advertising majority of revenue is not predictable beyond one year. Advertising agreements run one year or less and can be ended without penalty, the company discloses no advertiser or customer concentration, and visitors arrive through search, email and social referrals while the company says search rankings fluctuate and traffic cannot be assured, so that revenue is cyclical, discretionary and exposed to substitution rather than recurring. Advertising and performance marketing fell USD 35.8 million for nine months, led by USD 22.8 million in Technology & Shopping, USD 10.0 million in Health & Wellness and USD 3.0 million in Gaming & Entertainment, and retention fell in each. The credit implication is that the 63.09% of revenue that supports most of the EBITDA has little contractual protection in a downturn.

Pricing power is weak in advertising and mixed in subscriptions. Quarterly revenue per advertising customer fell to USD 109,111 from USD 132,849 in Technology & Shopping and to USD 57,224 from USD 74,053 in Gaming & Entertainment while customer counts rose, which means advertisers are spending less each, and it rose only in Health & Wellness, where customers fell to 723 from 825. In subscriptions, revenue per customer rose in Gaming & Entertainment and Health & Wellness and fell in Cybersecurity & Martech, while customers fell in all three, so price and mix are offsetting volume losses only in part; Health & Wellness customers fell 22.19%. A rising price per remaining customer cannot offset a shrinking base for long.

Costs did not flex with revenue. Sales and marketing was 43.1% of revenue against 41.4% and direct costs 15.8% against 14.3%, and the cost base of USD 697.3 million, operating costs before depreciation, amortization and goodwill impairment, was 4.39% higher than a year earlier while revenue fell 3.48%. Sales and marketing of USD 363.6 million is the main lever, but it consists primarily of internet-based advertising, so cutting it could lower traffic and revenue further. The credit implication is that margins cannot be defended at current revenue without a deliberate cost program, which the filings do not describe; no restructuring cost or program is stated.

### Competitive forces

Rivalry is intense and works on the revenue line. The company names diversified rivals such as IAC, Future PLC and Red Ventures, vertical specialists such as RVO Health, TechTarget and Vox Media, and large ad sellers such as Alphabet, Meta and Snap, some with greater resources. Falling retention in all three advertising segments is consistent with rivals and platforms taking budget, which lowers revenue and margin and the earnings that support refinancing.

The threat of new entrants is moderate on the evidence in the filings. The company says its markets are highly competitive and that rivals may have cheaper pricing or more effective marketing, and generative AI makes content easier to copy and reproduce, while established brands, audience reach and exclusive advertising representation for the properties of two medical centers slow entry. The effect on creditors is gradual traffic and pricing pressure rather than a sudden break, which is an analyst reading.

The threat of substitutes is the most credit-relevant force. The company states that generative AI may reduce its online traffic and audience sizes, and it has sued OpenAI for copying its content, with no recovery or loss amount stated. Lower traffic cuts advertising and affiliate commission revenue directly, with no contractual protection, so substitution would lower the earnings that support the notes before any cost response.

Buyer power is high in advertising and moderate in subscriptions. Advertisers can cancel without penalty and retention is falling, while subscribers are consumers and small businesses paying small monthly amounts, so they can leave but no single one matters; no concentration is disclosed. The implication is that pricing cannot be raised to cover cost increases.

Supplier power is high for traffic. Search engines, social platforms and ad exchanges control whether the company's pages are found and monetized, the company says search rankings fluctuate and algorithm changes can lower placement, and it has sued Google and Alphabet alleging antitrust violations related to publisher ad servers and ad exchanges. Partner payments and cloud costs add smaller supplier exposure, so a change by a platform can reduce revenue without any change in the company's own conduct.
### Macro, policy and technology factors

Technology and regulation are material to credit; macroeconomic and political factors matter through advertising budgets. Generative AI may reduce referral traffic, and the law on its use of copyrighted material is unsettled, which could cut revenue or, if the company's lawsuits succeed, add recoveries that the filings do not size. Privacy class actions against Mashable and IGN under California and federal privacy statutes carry no estimable loss and none is accrued, so an adverse ruling would be an unreserved call on cash. Advertising budgets are cyclical and discretionary, and the company notes that trade and tariff policy can cause cancellations. Interest rates are higher than when the notes were issued, and the company says it may not be able to refinance fixed-rate debt at similar rates.
### Credit-translated SWOT

Strengths that support the credit are cash above debt, a simple fixed-rate unsecured structure, no sponsor or dividend, and a subscription third of revenue; each is set out with its mechanism above. Weaknesses that constrain it are shrinking cancellable advertising revenue, falling margin, the use of cash for repurchases, goodwill at risk and a revolver that expires within a year.

### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next 12 months to 24 months the outlook is stable for liquidity and negative for earnings. Tailwinds are the cash balance, the removal of the 1.75% maturity, and interest income on cash that already exceeded interest expense in the third quarter. Headwinds are falling advertising retention, generative AI and search changes cutting traffic, the revolver expiry in June 2027, the 2028 convertible notes that holders can convert freely from December 2027, tax and fees on the sale gain, and a repurchase authorization that runs to 2036. Whether earnings recover depends on the fourth quarter, which in 2025 earned 34.97% of total-entity EBITDA.

Over the next three to five years the credit turns on whether the continuing portfolio stabilizes below its current size and whether the cash is applied to the 2028 and 2030 notes or to shareholders and acquisitions. The company has deployed about USD 3.3 billion on acquisitions since 2012 and calls programmatic acquisition a tenet of its strategy, so a return to acquisitions funded from sale cash is the main medium-term headwind, while a smaller note stack of USD 723.2 million is a tailwind if cash repays it. No company guidance is supplied.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_zd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation CALC-16
### Downside scenario

The downside begins with a further loss of search and AI referral traffic, the risk the company names for its audience and the pressure it cites for the Technology & Shopping decline, together with advertiser budget cuts that the one-year, cancellable agreements allow. The first operating break is in Technology & Shopping and Health & Wellness, where the reporting units with no excess fair value sit: advertising revenue falls faster than the 6.30% of nine months while the cost base, which rose 4.39%, stays near current levels, so EBITDA before goodwill impairment falls below the USD 41.6 million of the third quarter. The financial transmission is further non-cash impairments from the USD 872.8 million of goodwill with little or no headroom, lower covenant earnings if impairments are not added back, and free cash flow that stays negative as in the third quarter, when the combined outflow after capital expenditure was USD 100.07 million.

The liquidity consequence arrives through cash: at the third-quarter rate of fall of USD 198.4 million cash would last 7.09 quarters before the USD 279.95 million of near claims, so continued repurchases with a negative operating cash flow would leave the 2028 convertible notes of USD 263.1 million to be met from a much smaller cash balance, an illustration and not a forecast. The leverage and refinancing consequence is that the revolver would need to be extended in mid-2027 on a covenant package tested against lower earnings, and debt principal is already at least 3.64x the only earnings bound available. Management has several levers: it can stop repurchases, which were USD 92.0 million in the third quarter, cut sales and marketing of USD 363.6 million, defer capital expenditure, repay or repurchase notes below par, or sell further businesses. Resilience is sufficient to avoid liquidity distress within 24 months because those levers are within management's control and cash is large; it is not sufficient if repurchases and acquisitions continue while earnings fall. Observable triggers are advertising retention below 85%, quarterly EBITDA before goodwill impairment below USD 41.6 million, cash below USD 1,000 million, no revolver extension by March 2027, and repurchases above USD 92.0 million in a quarter.

### Overall credit view

Overall, Ziff Davis presents an adequate business profile supported by cash of USD 535.4 million above debt principal, with pro forma cash after the 1.75% repayment not established, an undrawn revolver, fixed-rate unsecured debt with no drawn maturity before March 2028 after that repayment, and no sponsor or dividend, but credit quality is constrained by shrinking, cancellable advertising revenue, a margin that fell to 17.35% from 23.59% before goodwill impairment, USD 872.8 million of goodwill with little or no headroom and a policy of returning cash to shareholders. Cash-flow durability appears weak because free cash flow was an outflow of USD 49.3 million for nine months on the combined basis and 69.91% of EBITDA converted to free cash flow only in FY2025 with Connectivity included. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on extending the revolver before its June 2027 expiry, on earnings recovering in the fourth quarter, and on how much of the sale cash remains by March 2028. The primary downside path is traffic and advertiser losses that lower earnings while cash is spent. A comparison with typical leveraged-credit issuers in the sector is not established because no peer set is supplied. Further analysis would require recast continuing-basis annual results, the executed credit agreement and covenant definitions, the date and effect of the 1.75% repayment and tax payment, and management guidance. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: shareholder returns and falling advertising earnings eroding the sale cash before the 2028 convertible notes and the revolver renewal.
